topics.title: Sounds, spelling and stress
topics.md:
Spanish spelling is very regular: once you know the rules, you can pronounce almost any word you see — and spell almost any word you hear. Click the examples to hear them.

## Vowels

Spanish has only **five vowel sounds**, and they are always short and pure (no "glide" like English *say* or *go*).

| letter | sound | example |
|---|---|---|
| a | like *a* in *father* | [[casa]] |
| e | like *e* in *bet* | [[mesa]] |
| i | like *ee* in *see* (short) | [[sí]] |
| o | like *o* in *not*, rounded | [[todo]] |
| u | like *oo* in *food* (short) | [[uno]] |

## Consonants that differ from English

| letter | how to say it | examples |
|---|---|---|
| **h** | always silent | [[hola]], [[hombre]] |
| **j**, **g** before e/i | a rough *h* from the throat | [[jamón]], [[gente]] |
| **g** before a/o/u | hard *g* as in *go* | [[gato]], [[amigo]] |
| **gue, gui** | hard *g*, the *u* is silent | [[guitarra]] |
| **c** before e/i, **z** | *th* in Spain, *s* in Latin America | [[cinco]], [[zapato]] |
| **c** before a/o/u, **qu** | *k* | [[casa]], [[queso]] |
| **ll**, **y** | like *y* in *yes* | [[calle]], [[yo]] |
| **ñ** | like *ny* in *canyon* | [[España]], [[mañana]] |
| **r** | a single tap of the tongue (like *tt* in American *butter*) | [[pero]] |
| **rr**, or **r** at the start of a word | a rolled, trilled *r* | [[perro]], [[rojo]] |
| **v** | same as **b** | [[vino]], [[bien]] |
| **d** between vowels | soft, like *th* in *this* | [[nada]] |

> Compare [[pero]] (but) and [[perro]] (dog): one tap vs. a trill changes the meaning.

## Where the stress goes

1. Words ending in a **vowel, -n or -s** are stressed on the **second-to-last** syllable: [[casa]], [[hablan]], [[libros]].
2. Words ending in **any other consonant** are stressed on the **last** syllable: [[hablar]], [[ciudad]], [[español]].
3. If a word breaks these rules, it gets a **written accent** on the stressed vowel: [[café]], [[lápiz]], [[música]], [[canción]].

Accents also distinguish words that are otherwise identical: [[tú]] (you) / [[tu]] (your), [[sí]] (yes) / [[si]] (if), [[él]] (he) / [[el]] (the), [[qué]] (what?) / [[que]] (that).

## Punctuation

Questions and exclamations are framed with an upside-down mark at the start: [[¿Cómo estás?]] [[¡Hola!]]

## Greetings

| Spanish | English |
|---|---|
| [[Hola]] | Hello / Hi |
| [[Buenos días]] | Good morning |
| [[Buenas tardes]] | Good afternoon / evening |
| [[Buenas noches]] | Good evening / night |
| [[¿Qué tal?]] | How are you? / How's it going? |
| [[Bien, gracias.]] | Fine, thanks. |
| [[Mucho gusto.]] | Nice to meet you. |
| [[Adiós]] / [[Hasta luego]] | Goodbye / See you later |
| [[Por favor]] / [[Gracias]] / [[De nada]] | Please / Thank you / You're welcome |
| [[Perdón]] / [[Lo siento]] | Excuse me / I'm sorry |

topics.title: Subject pronouns and ser (to be)
topics.md:
## Subject pronouns

| | singular | plural |
|---|---|---|
| 1st | [[yo]] — I | [[nosotros]] / [[nosotras]] — we |
| 2nd (informal) | [[tú]] — you | [[vosotros]] / [[vosotras]] — you all (Spain) |
| 2nd (formal) | [[usted]] — you | [[ustedes]] — you all |
| 3rd | [[él]] — he, [[ella]] — she | [[ellos]] / [[ellas]] — they |

- **tú** is for friends, family, children, people your age. **usted** (often written *Ud.*) is polite: strangers, older people, formal situations. Grammatically, *usted* takes the **he/she** form of the verb.
- In Latin America **ustedes** is the only plural "you" (both friendly and formal). In Spain, **vosotros** is the friendly plural.
- The **-as** forms (*nosotras, vosotras, ellas*) are for groups of only women; any mixed group uses the masculine.
- Spanish usually **drops** subject pronouns because the verb ending already shows the person: [[Soy estudiante.]] = I am a student. Use the pronoun for emphasis or contrast: [[Yo soy de Madrid, y él es de Lima.]]

## Ser — "to be" (identity)

| | |
|---|---|
| yo **soy** | nosotros **somos** |
| tú **eres** | vosotros **sois** |
| él / ella / usted **es** | ellos / ellas / ustedes **son** |

Use **ser** for what something *is* — things that define it:

- **identity, name**: [[Soy Ana.]] [[Es mi hermano.]]
- **profession**: [[Ella es médica.]] (no *una* before a profession!)
- **origin, nationality** (with *de*): [[Somos de México.]] [[¿De dónde eres?]]
- **characteristics**: [[El libro es interesante.]]
- **time and dates**: [[Son las tres.]] [[Hoy es lunes.]]
- **material**: [[La mesa es de madera.]]

> Spanish has a second verb "to be", **estar**, for location and temporary states. You will meet it in a few units.

## Negation and questions

Put **no** before the verb: [[No soy profesor.]] For a yes/no question, just use question marks and rising intonation: [[¿Eres estudiante?]] — [[Sí, soy estudiante.]] / [[No, no soy estudiante.]]

## Introducing yourself

| | |
|---|---|
| [[¿Cómo te llamas?]] | What's your name? (lit. how do you call yourself?) |
| [[Me llamo Pablo.]] | My name is Pablo. |
| [[¿De dónde eres?]] | Where are you from? |
| [[Soy de Inglaterra.]] | I'm from England. |

drills.h: What's your name? — My name is Ana.

topics.title: Nouns: gender, plural and articles
topics.md:
## Every noun has a gender

In Spanish every noun is **masculine** or **feminine** — even objects and ideas. The gender decides the form of articles and adjectives, so **always learn a noun together with its article**: not *casa* but [[la casa]].

| usually masculine | usually feminine |
|---|---|
| ending in **-o**: [[el libro]], [[el perro]] | ending in **-a**: [[la casa]], [[la mesa]] |
| ending in **-or**: [[el ordenador]] | ending in **-ción, -sión**: [[la canción]] |
| ending in **-aje**: [[el viaje]] | ending in **-dad, -tad**: [[la ciudad]], [[la libertad]] |
| | ending in **-umbre**: [[la costumbre]] |

Important exceptions you'll meet early:

- [[el día]], [[el mapa]], [[el problema]], [[el idioma]], [[el sistema]], [[el programa]] — masculine despite **-a** (many words in *-ma* are Greek and masculine).
- [[la mano]], [[la foto]] (= fotografía), [[la radio]], [[la moto]] — feminine despite **-o**.
- Nouns ending in **-e** or another consonant can be either: [[el coche]], [[la noche]], [[el hotel]], [[la flor]]. Just learn them.

For people, the gender usually follows the person: [[el niño]] / [[la niña]], [[el profesor]] / [[la profesora]], [[el estudiante]] / [[la estudiante]].

## The definite article — "the"

| | singular | plural |
|---|---|---|
| masculine | **el** libro | **los** libros |
| feminine | **la** casa | **las** casas |

A mixed group is masculine: [[los padres]] = the parents (father + mother).

> **el agua**: feminine nouns that begin with a **stressed a-** take *el* in the singular to avoid two *a* sounds clashing: [[el agua]], [[el alma]], [[el área]]. They are still feminine: [[el agua fría]], [[las aguas]].

Spanish uses *the* more than English — for general statements and with abstract nouns: [[Me gusta el café.]] (I like coffee), [[La vida es bella.]] (Life is beautiful).

## Plural

| ending | rule | example |
|---|---|---|
| vowel | add **-s** | [[libro]] → [[libros]] |
| consonant | add **-es** | [[ciudad]] → [[ciudades]], [[papel]] → [[papeles]] |
| **-z** | **-z → -ces** | [[lápiz]] → [[lápices]], [[vez]] → [[veces]] |
| **-ión** | add -es, drop the accent | [[canción]] → [[canciones]] |

## Contractions

**a + el = al**, **de + el = del**: [[Voy al parque.]] [[Es el coche del profesor.]] (but *a la*, *de la* don't contract).

topics.title: Un, una, unos, unas
topics.md:
## "A / an" and "some"

| | singular | plural |
|---|---|---|
| masculine | **un** libro — a book | **unos** libros — some books |
| feminine | **una** casa — a house | **unas** casas — some houses |

- [[Tengo un perro y una gata.]] — I have a dog and a (female) cat.
- [[Hay unos libros en la mesa.]] — There are some books on the table.
- *unos / unas* before a number means "about": [[unos veinte euros]] — about twenty euros.

Like *el*, **un** is used before feminine nouns with a stressed *a-*: [[un águila]], [[un hacha]].

## When Spanish leaves the article out

1. **Professions, nationality, religion after *ser*** (unless there is an adjective):
   [[Soy profesor.]] — I am **a** teacher. But: [[Es un profesor muy bueno.]]
2. After **tener** / **buscar** / **llevar** when the number doesn't matter, especially in questions and negatives:
   [[¿Tienes coche?]] — Do you have a car? [[No tengo hermanos.]]
3. Before **otro** (another), **cien**, **mil**, **medio**: [[otro café]] = another coffee (never *un otro*), [[mil euros]].

## When to use *el* vs *un*

*un/una* introduces something new or non-specific; *el/la* refers to something known or unique:
[[Hay un restaurante en la calle. El restaurante es muy bueno.]]

drills.h: There is a cat in the street.

topics.title: Adjectives: agreement and position
topics.md:
## Agreement

Adjectives **agree** with the noun in gender and number.

| ending | masc. sing. | fem. sing. | masc. pl. | fem. pl. |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| **-o** | [[alto]] | [[alta]] | [[altos]] | [[altas]] |
| **-e** | [[grande]] | grande | [[grandes]] | grandes |
| consonant | [[fácil]] | fácil | [[fáciles]] | fáciles |
| nationality (consonant) | [[español]] | [[española]] | [[españoles]] | [[españolas]] |

- [[El chico es alto.]] / [[La chica es alta.]] / [[Los chicos son altos.]] / [[Las chicas son altas.]]
- A mixed group → masculine plural: [[Juan y María son simpáticos.]]
- Adjectives in *-or* add *-a*: [[trabajador]] → [[trabajadora]].

## Position

Most adjectives go **after** the noun — the opposite of English:
[[un coche rojo]] (a red car), [[una ciudad grande]], [[un libro interesante]].

Some common adjectives usually come **before**: [[mucho]], [[poco]], [[otro]], numbers, and *bueno / malo* often do:
[[mucho tiempo]], [[otra vez]], [[un buen día]].

**Short forms** before a masculine singular noun:

| | |
|---|---|
| bueno → **buen** | [[un buen amigo]] |
| malo → **mal** | [[un mal día]] |
| primero → **primer** | [[el primer día]] |
| grande → **gran** (before any singular noun) | [[una gran ciudad]] = a great city |

> **grande** changes meaning with position: [[una ciudad grande]] = a big city; [[una gran ciudad]] = a great city.

## Muy

**muy** = very, and never changes: [[muy alto]], [[muy alta]], [[muy altos]].

topics.title: Estar, and ser vs estar (basics)
topics.md:
## Estar — the other "to be"

| | |
|---|---|
| yo **estoy** | nosotros **estamos** |
| tú **estás** | vosotros **estáis** |
| él / ella / usted **está** | ellos / ellas / ustedes **están** |

Use **estar** for:

- **location** (where something/someone is): [[Estoy en casa.]] [[¿Dónde está el baño?]] [[Madrid está en España.]]
- **states and conditions** (how something is *right now*): [[Estoy cansado.]] [[La sopa está fría.]] [[¿Cómo estás? — Estoy bien.]]
- **ongoing actions**: *estar + -ando/-iendo* (you'll learn it later): [[Estoy comiendo.]]

## Ser or estar?

A simple rule of thumb: **ser = what it is**, **estar = how / where it is**.

| ser (identity, characteristics) | estar (location, state, result) |
|---|---|
| [[Ana es alta.]] — Ana is tall. | [[Ana está cansada.]] — Ana is tired. |
| [[Es médico.]] — He's a doctor. | [[Está en el hospital.]] — He's at the hospital. |
| [[La fiesta es en mi casa.]] — The party is (takes place) at my house. | [[Mi casa está en el centro.]] — My house is in the centre. |
| [[Es aburrido.]] — He's boring. | [[Está aburrido.]] — He's bored. |
| [[Es listo.]] — He's clever. | [[Está listo.]] — He's ready. |

> Location of **things and people** → *estar*. Location of **events** (a party, a concert, a meeting) → *ser*.

Some adjectives change meaning — you'll study more of these at B2. For now remember *aburrido, listo, malo* (ser malo = to be bad; estar malo = to be ill).

**Feelings and moods** almost always take *estar*: [[contento]], [[triste]], [[enfadado]], [[nervioso]], [[preocupado]], [[ocupado]]. But **feliz** is usually used with *ser*: [[Soy feliz.]]

## Useful phrases

- [[¿Dónde está…?]] — Where is…?
- [[Está aquí / allí / ahí.]] — It's here / over there / there (near you).
- [[Está cerca / lejos.]] — It's near / far.
- [[La tienda está abierta / cerrada.]] — The shop is open / closed.

topics.title: Hay and numbers 0–100
topics.md:
## Hay — there is / there are

**hay** (from *haber*) means both *there is* and *there are*. It never changes for plural.

- [[Hay un banco en la calle.]] — There is a bank in the street.
- [[Hay tres libros en la mesa.]] — There are three books on the table.
- [[¿Hay leche?]] — Is there any milk? [[No hay pan.]] — There's no bread.

**hay** introduces things that are new or unspecified (with *un, una, unos, numbers, mucho*, or no article). To say where a *specific* thing is, use **estar**:

| hay | estar |
|---|---|
| [[Hay un hotel cerca.]] — There's a hotel nearby. | [[El hotel está cerca.]] — The hotel is nearby. |

**hay que** + infinitive = one has to: [[Hay que estudiar.]]

## Numbers 0–100

| | | | |
|---|---|---|---|
| 0 [[cero]] | 1 [[uno]] | 2 [[dos]] | 3 [[tres]] |
| 4 [[cuatro]] | 5 [[cinco]] | 6 [[seis]] | 7 [[siete]] |
| 8 [[ocho]] | 9 [[nueve]] | 10 [[diez]] | 11 [[once]] |
| 12 [[doce]] | 13 [[trece]] | 14 [[catorce]] | 15 [[quince]] |
| 16 [[dieciséis]] | 17 [[diecisiete]] | 18 [[dieciocho]] | 19 [[diecinueve]] |
| 20 [[veinte]] | 21 [[veintiuno]] | 22 [[veintidós]] | 30 [[treinta]] |
| 40 [[cuarenta]] | 50 [[cincuenta]] | 60 [[sesenta]] | 70 [[setenta]] |
| 80 [[ochenta]] | 90 [[noventa]] | 100 [[cien]] | 101 [[ciento uno]] |

- 16–29 are written as one word: *dieciséis, veinticinco*.
- From 31 on, use **y**: [[treinta y uno]], [[cuarenta y cinco]], [[noventa y nueve]].
- **uno** becomes **un** before a masculine noun and **una** before a feminine one: [[veintiún años]], [[treinta y una casas]].
- **cien** = exactly 100 (*cien euros*); **ciento** in 101–199 (*ciento veinte*).

## How many?

**¿Cuánto?** agrees with the noun: [[¿Cuántos años tienes?]] (How old are you?), [[¿Cuántas personas hay?]], [[¿Cuánto cuesta?]] (How much is it?).

topics.title: Tener and expressions with tener
topics.md:
## Tener — to have

| | |
|---|---|
| yo **tengo** | nosotros **tenemos** |
| tú **tienes** | vosotros **tenéis** |
| él / ella / usted **tiene** | ellos / ellas / ustedes **tienen** |

*Tener* is irregular: **tengo** in the *yo* form, and **e → ie** in the stressed forms (*tienes, tiene, tienen*).

- [[Tengo dos hermanos.]] — I have two brothers.
- [[¿Tienes coche?]] — Do you have a car?
- [[No tenemos tiempo.]] — We don't have time.

## Age: tener … años

Spanish *has* years: [[Tengo veinte años.]] — I'm twenty. [[¿Cuántos años tienes?]] — How old are you?

## Expressions with tener (English uses "to be")

| Spanish | English |
|---|---|
| [[tener hambre]] | to be hungry |
| [[tener sed]] | to be thirsty |
| [[tener frío]] / [[tener calor]] | to be cold / hot (a person) |
| [[tener sueño]] | to be sleepy |
| [[tener miedo]] (de) | to be afraid (of) |
| [[tener razón]] | to be right |
| [[tener prisa]] | to be in a hurry |
| [[tener suerte]] | to be lucky |
| [[tener cuidado]] | to be careful |
| [[tener ganas de]] + inf. | to feel like doing |

These are **nouns**, so "very" is **mucho/mucha**, not *muy*: [[Tengo mucha hambre.]] [[Tengo mucho frío.]]

## Tener que — to have to

**tener que + infinitive** = to have to (obligation): [[Tengo que trabajar.]] — I have to work. [[¿Tienes que irte?]] — Do you have to go?

topics.title: Present tense: regular -ar verbs
topics.md:
## Three verb families

Spanish infinitives end in **-ar**, **-er** or **-ir**. To conjugate a regular verb, remove the ending to get the **stem** and add the personal endings. The ending tells you who is doing the action, so the pronoun is usually dropped.

## -ar verbs: hablar (to speak)

| | ending | |
|---|---|---|
| yo | **-o** | [[hablo]] |
| tú | **-as** | [[hablas]] |
| él / ella / usted | **-a** | [[habla]] |
| nosotros | **-amos** | [[hablamos]] |
| vosotros | **-áis** | [[habláis]] |
| ellos / ellas / ustedes | **-an** | [[hablan]] |

Most Spanish verbs are **-ar** verbs and most of them are regular: *trabajar, estudiar, comprar, llamar, tomar, llegar, mirar, escuchar, esperar, necesitar, ayudar, cocinar, bailar, cantar, pagar, viajar*.

- [[Hablo inglés y un poco de español.]]
- [[¿Trabajas aquí?]]
- [[Mi padre cocina muy bien.]]
- [[Estudiamos español los lunes.]]
- [[¿Qué buscáis?]]
- [[Ellos llegan mañana.]]

## What the present tense covers

The Spanish present is used for:

1. Habits and facts: [[Trabajo en una oficina.]] — I work in an office.
2. Actions happening now: [[¿Qué miras?]] — What are you looking at?
3. The near future (with a time word): [[Mañana compro el pan.]] — I'll buy the bread tomorrow.
4. Offers / requests: [[¿Te ayudo?]] — Shall I help you?

> English *do / does* doesn't exist here: [[¿Hablas español?]] = Do you speak Spanish? [[No hablo alemán.]] = I don't speak German.

## Spelling notes

- **llegar → llego, pagar → pago** (regular in the present; spelling changes only appear later in the past tense).
- The stress falls on the stem in *hablo, hablas, habla, hablan* and on the ending in *hablamos, habláis*.

topics.title: Present tense: regular -er and -ir verbs
topics.md:
## -er and -ir verbs

The endings are almost the same: **-er** and **-ir** verbs differ only in the *nosotros* and *vosotros* forms.

| | comer (to eat) | vivir (to live) |
|---|---|---|
| yo | [[como]] | [[vivo]] |
| tú | [[comes]] | [[vives]] |
| él / ella / usted | [[come]] | [[vive]] |
| nosotros | [[comemos]] | [[vivimos]] |
| vosotros | [[coméis]] | [[vivís]] |
| ellos / ellas / ustedes | [[comen]] | [[viven]] |

**Regular -er verbs:** beber, leer, aprender, comprender, correr, creer, vender, deber.
**Regular -ir verbs:** vivir, escribir, abrir, recibir, subir, decidir, compartir, existir.

- [[¿Dónde vives?]] — Where do you live?
- [[Leo un libro cada semana.]]
- [[Mis hijos comen mucha fruta.]]
- [[Escribimos correos en español.]]
- [[No comprendo la pregunta.]]
- [[Debes descansar.]] — You should rest. (*deber* + infinitive = should / must)

## Summary of present endings

| | -ar | -er | -ir |
|---|---|---|---|
| yo | -o | -o | -o |
| tú | -as | -es | -es |
| él/ella/Ud. | -a | -e | -e |
| nosotros | -amos | -emos | **-imos** |
| vosotros | -áis | -éis | **-ís** |
| ellos/Uds. | -an | -en | -en |

> A quick way to remember: -er/-ir verbs swap the **a** of -ar verbs for **e**.

**leer** and **creer** are regular in the present: [[leo]], [[lees]], [[creo]], [[crees]]. (*Ver* is slightly irregular: **veo**, ves, ve…)

topics.title: Questions and negation
topics.md:
## Question words

All question words carry a **written accent** — both in direct and indirect questions.

| | |
|---|---|
| [[¿Qué?]] | What? Which? |
| [[¿Quién?]] / [[¿Quiénes?]] | Who? (sing. / pl.) |
| [[¿Dónde?]] | Where? — [[¿Adónde?]] Where to? — [[¿De dónde?]] Where from? |
| [[¿Cuándo?]] | When? |
| [[¿Cómo?]] | How? (also: Pardon?) |
| [[¿Cuánto?]] / [[¿Cuánta?]] / [[¿Cuántos?]] / [[¿Cuántas?]] | How much? / How many? |
| [[¿Cuál?]] / [[¿Cuáles?]] | Which (one)? What? |
| [[¿Por qué?]] | Why? — answer: [[porque]] = because |

- [[¿Qué haces?]] — What are you doing?
- [[¿Quién es ella?]] — Who is she?
- [[¿Cómo te llamas?]] — What's your name?
- [[¿Por qué estudias español? — Porque me gusta.]]

**Qué vs cuál** before *ser*: use **cuál** to ask for one item from a set, **qué** to ask for a definition.
[[¿Cuál es tu número de teléfono?]] (What's your phone number?) vs [[¿Qué es un móvil?]] (What is a "móvil"?)

**Prepositions go first**: [[¿De dónde eres?]] (Where are you from?), [[¿Con quién vives?]] (Who do you live with?), [[¿Para qué?]] (What for?).

## Word order in questions

The verb usually comes right after the question word, and the subject (if any) after the verb:
[[¿Dónde vive tu hermano?]] — Where does your brother live?

## Negation

- **no** goes before the verb: [[No trabajo los domingos.]]
- Double negatives are normal: **no** + verb + *nada / nadie / nunca*:
  [[No veo nada.]] — I don't see anything. [[No hay nadie.]] — There's nobody. [[No como nunca carne.]] = [[Nunca como carne.]]
- **también** (also) ↔ **tampoco** (neither): [[Yo también.]] / [[Yo tampoco.]]

topics.title: Possessive adjectives (mi, tu, su…)
topics.md:
## My, your, his, our…

| owner | singular thing | plural things |
|---|---|---|
| yo | **mi** casa | **mis** casas |
| tú | **tu** casa | **tus** casas |
| él / ella / usted | **su** casa | **sus** casas |
| nosotros | **nuestro** coche / **nuestra** casa | **nuestros** coches / **nuestras** casas |
| vosotros | **vuestro** coche / **vuestra** casa | **vuestros** / **vuestras** |
| ellos / ellas / ustedes | **su** casa | **sus** casas |

Possessive adjectives agree with the **thing owned**, not with the owner:

- [[mis padres]] — my parents (one owner, many parents → plural)
- [[nuestra madre]] — our mother (*nuestra* because *madre* is feminine)
- [[sus hijos]] — his / her / their / your children

**tu** (your) has no accent; **tú** (you) has one: [[Tú tienes tu libro.]]

## Su is ambiguous

*su* can mean his, her, its, their or your (usted/ustedes). If context isn't clear, use **de + person**:
[[Es su coche.]] → [[Es el coche de Ana.]] / [[Es el coche de ellos.]] / [[Es el coche de usted.]]

## Possession with de

Spanish has no *'s*: **the noun + de + owner**.
- [[el libro de Pedro]] — Pedro's book
- [[la casa de mis padres]] — my parents' house

## Family vocabulary

[[el padre]] / [[la madre]] — father / mother · [[los padres]] — parents · [[el hermano]] / [[la hermana]] — brother / sister · [[el hijo]] / [[la hija]] — son / daughter · [[el abuelo]] / [[la abuela]] — grandfather / grandmother · [[el tío]] / [[la tía]] — uncle / aunt · [[el primo]] / [[la prima]] — cousin · [[el esposo]] / [[la esposa]] — husband / wife · [[el novio]] / [[la novia]] — boyfriend / girlfriend

> Masculine plurals cover mixed groups: [[mis hermanos]] can mean "my brothers" or "my brothers and sisters".

topics.title: Demonstratives: este, ese, aquel
topics.md:
## This, that, that over there

Spanish has **three** distances:

| | near me | near you | far from both |
|---|---|---|---|
| masc. sing. | [[este]] libro | [[ese]] libro | [[aquel]] libro |
| fem. sing. | [[esta]] casa | [[esa]] casa | [[aquella]] casa |
| masc. pl. | [[estos]] libros | [[esos]] libros | [[aquellos]] libros |
| fem. pl. | [[estas]] casas | [[esas]] casas | [[aquellas]] casas |

The adverbs match: [[aquí]] (here) ↔ *este*, [[ahí]] (there, near you) ↔ *ese*, [[allí]] / [[allá]] (over there) ↔ *aquel*.

- [[Este café está frío.]] — This coffee is cold.
- [[¿Cuánto cuesta esa camisa?]] — How much is that shirt (the one you're holding)?
- [[Aquella montaña es muy alta.]] — That mountain over there is very high.

In everyday speech **ese** is used for most "that"; **aquel** is for clearly distant things or the distant past: [[en aquella época]] — in those days.

## As pronouns

The same words work alone, meaning *this one / that one*: [[Quiero este, no ese.]] — I want this one, not that one. (Old spelling with accents — *éste, ése* — is no longer required.)

## Neuter: esto, eso, aquello

For an unknown thing, an idea or a whole situation (never for a specific noun):
- [[¿Qué es esto?]] — What is this?
- [[Eso es verdad.]] — That's true.
- [[Por eso.]] — That's why.

Time expressions: [[este año]], [[esta semana]], [[esta noche]] (tonight), [[esta mañana]] (this morning).

drills.h: I want this one, not that one.

topics.title: Gustar and similar verbs
topics.md:
## How gustar works

**gustar** doesn't mean "to like" — it means "to please". The thing you like is the **subject**, and the person who likes it is an **indirect object** (*me, te, le…*).

[[Me gusta el café.]] = Coffee pleases me = I like coffee.

| indirect object | singular thing / verb | plural things |
|---|---|---|
| (a mí) **me** | gusta | gustan |
| (a ti) **te** | gusta | gustan |
| (a él / ella / usted) **le** | gusta | gustan |
| (a nosotros) **nos** | gusta | gustan |
| (a vosotros) **os** | gusta | gustan |
| (a ellos / ellas / ustedes) **les** | gusta | gustan |

So the verb is almost always **gusta** or **gustan**:

- [[Me gusta la música.]] — I like music. (one thing)
- [[Me gustan los perros.]] — I like dogs. (plural)
- [[Nos gusta bailar.]] — We like dancing. (infinitives are singular)
- [[¿Te gustan las películas de terror?]]
- [[No le gusta el pescado.]] — He/she doesn't like fish.

## Adding a mí, a ti, a Juan…

The phrase **a + person** adds emphasis or clarifies who *le / les* is. The pronoun stays!
- [[A mí me gusta el té, pero a ella le gusta el café.]]
- [[A Juan le gustan los coches.]]
- [[¿A ti te gusta? — A mí sí. / A mí no.]]
- Agreeing: [[A mí también.]] / [[A mí tampoco.]]

## Encantar — to love (things)

**encantar** works the same way and is stronger: [[Me encanta España.]] [[Nos encantan tus fotos.]] Don't add *mucho* to *encantar*.

> To say you love a **person**, use *querer*: [[Te quiero.]] — I love you.

## Degrees

[[Me gusta mucho.]] (I like it a lot) · [[No me gusta nada.]] (I don't like it at all) · [[Me gusta más el té.]] (I prefer tea).

drills.q: A mis padres ___ gustan las películas.

drills.h: I don't like it at all.
Make it plural: "I like the books."

topics.title: Telling the time, days and dates
topics.md:
## What time is it?

[[¿Qué hora es?]] — What time is it? Use **ser** with the article **la / las** (*hora* is feminine):

| | |
|---|---|
| 1:00 | [[Es la una.]] |
| 2:00 | [[Son las dos.]] |
| 3:05 | [[Son las tres y cinco.]] |
| 4:15 | [[Son las cuatro y cuarto.]] |
| 5:30 | [[Son las cinco y media.]] |
| 6:40 | [[Son las siete menos veinte.]] (7 minus 20) |
| 8:45 | [[Son las nueve menos cuarto.]] |
| 12:00 | [[Es mediodía.]] / [[Es medianoche.]] |

- Only *one o'clock* is singular: **es la una**; everything else is **son las…**
- At a time: **a la / a las**: [[La clase es a las diez.]] [[¿A qué hora abre?]]
- Parts of the day: [[de la mañana]] (a.m.), [[de la tarde]] (afternoon/early evening), [[de la noche]] (night): [[a las ocho de la tarde]].
- Without a clock time: [[por la mañana]], [[por la tarde]], [[por la noche]] — in the morning / afternoon / at night.

## Days of the week

[[lunes]], [[martes]], [[miércoles]], [[jueves]], [[viernes]], [[sábado]], [[domingo]] — lowercase, masculine.

- **el** + day = on that day: [[El lunes tengo clase.]] — On Monday I have class.
- **los** + day = every week: [[Los domingos como con mi familia.]] — On Sundays…
- [[el fin de semana]] — the weekend

## Months and dates

[[enero]], [[febrero]], [[marzo]], [[abril]], [[mayo]], [[junio]], [[julio]], [[agosto]], [[septiembre]], [[octubre]], [[noviembre]], [[diciembre]] — lowercase.

Dates use cardinal numbers (except *primero* is common for the 1st in Latin America):
[[Hoy es el doce de octubre.]] — Today is the 12th of October. [[Nací el tres de mayo de 1995.]] [[¿Qué día es hoy?]]

## Time words

[[hoy]] (today) · [[mañana]] (tomorrow) · [[ayer]] (yesterday) · [[pasado mañana]] (the day after tomorrow) · [[la semana que viene]] (next week) · [[temprano]] (early) · [[tarde]] (late)

> **mañana** = tomorrow, **la mañana** = the morning: [[mañana por la mañana]] — tomorrow morning.

topics.title: Reflexive verbs and daily routine
topics.md:
## Reflexive verbs

A reflexive verb has **-se** attached to the infinitive: [[levantarse]] (to get up), [[llamarse]] (to be called). The action "comes back" to the subject. Conjugate the verb normally and put the matching **reflexive pronoun** before it:

| | levantarse |
|---|---|
| yo | **me** levanto |
| tú | **te** levantas |
| él / ella / usted | **se** levanta |
| nosotros | **nos** levantamos |
| vosotros | **os** levantáis |
| ellos / ellas / ustedes | **se** levantan |

- [[Me levanto a las siete.]] — I get up at seven.
- [[¿A qué hora te acuestas?]] — What time do you go to bed?
- [[Mi hijo se ducha por la noche.]]
- [[Nos llamamos Ana y Luis.]] — Our names are Ana and Luis.

## Where does the pronoun go?

- **Before a conjugated verb**: [[Me ducho.]] [[No me ducho.]]
- **Attached to an infinitive or gerund** (or before the first verb — both are correct):
  [[Voy a ducharme.]] = [[Me voy a duchar.]] — I'm going to shower.
  [[Tienes que levantarte.]] = [[Te tienes que levantar.]]

## Daily routine vocabulary

| | |
|---|---|
| [[despertarse]] (e→ie) | to wake up — *me despierto* |
| [[levantarse]] | to get up |
| [[ducharse]] | to shower |
| [[lavarse]] los dientes / las manos | to brush one's teeth / wash one's hands |
| [[vestirse]] (e→i) | to get dressed — *me visto* |
| [[peinarse]] | to comb one's hair |
| [[acostarse]] (o→ue) | to go to bed — *me acuesto* |
| [[sentarse]] (e→ie) | to sit down — *me siento* |
| [[irse]] | to leave — *me voy* |

> With body parts Spanish uses **the**, not *my*: [[Me lavo las manos.]] — I wash my hands.

## Reflexive changes meaning

Some verbs mean something different with *se*: [[ir]] (to go) / [[irse]] (to leave); [[dormir]] (to sleep) / [[dormirse]] (to fall asleep); [[llamar]] (to call) / [[llamarse]] (to be called); [[quedar]] (to arrange to meet) / [[quedarse]] (to stay).

topics.title: Ir, ir a + infinitive, al / del
topics.md:
## Ir — to go

| | |
|---|---|
| yo **voy** | nosotros **vamos** |
| tú **vas** | vosotros **vais** |
| él / ella / usted **va** | ellos / ellas / ustedes **van** |

**ir** is completely irregular, but its present looks like an *-ar* verb with the stem *v-*.

## Ir a + place

Destination takes **a**, and **a + el = al**:
- [[Voy a Madrid.]] — I'm going to Madrid.
- [[Vamos al cine.]] — We're going to the cinema.
- [[¿Vas a la playa?]]
- [[¿Adónde vas?]] — Where are you going?

Note: **ir a casa** — to go home (no article). **ir de compras / de vacaciones / de viaje** — to go shopping / on holiday / on a trip.

Transport uses **en**: [[en tren]], [[en autobús]], [[en coche]], [[en avión]] — but **a pie** (on foot).

## Ir a + infinitive: the near future

**ir a + infinitive** = *going to*. It is the most common way to talk about plans in everyday Spanish.
- [[Voy a estudiar esta noche.]] — I'm going to study tonight.
- [[¿Qué vas a hacer mañana?]] — What are you going to do tomorrow?
- [[Va a llover.]] — It's going to rain.
- [[No vamos a salir.]]

**¡Vamos!** = Let's go! **Vamos a + infinitive** can also mean *let's…*: [[¡Vamos a comer!]]

## Al and del

| | |
|---|---|
| a + el = **al** | [[Voy al parque.]] |
| de + el = **del** | [[Vengo del trabajo.]] |
| a la, de la, a los, de las… | no contraction |

> Only the article **el** contracts, never the pronoun **él** (he): [[Es el coche de él.]] — It's his car.

drills.h: What are you going to do?

topics.title: Stem-changing verbs (e→ie, o→ue, e→i)
topics.md:
## Stem-changing ("boot") verbs

In many common verbs, the **stressed vowel of the stem changes** in the present tense. The change happens in every form **except nosotros and vosotros** (where the stress falls on the ending). If you draw a line around the changing forms in the table, it looks like a boot — hence the name.

| | e → ie: querer | o → ue: poder | e → i: pedir |
|---|---|---|---|
| yo | qu**ie**ro | p**ue**do | p**i**do |
| tú | qu**ie**res | p**ue**des | p**i**des |
| él/ella/Ud. | qu**ie**re | p**ue**de | p**i**de |
| nosotros | queremos | podemos | pedimos |
| vosotros | queréis | podéis | pedís |
| ellos/Uds. | qu**ie**ren | p**ue**den | p**i**den |

**e → ie**: [[querer]] (want), [[pensar]] (think), [[empezar]] (begin), [[entender]] (understand), [[preferir]] (prefer), [[cerrar]] (close), [[perder]] (lose), [[sentir]] (feel), [[tener]] and [[venir]] (+ irregular *yo*).

**o → ue**: [[poder]] (can), [[dormir]] (sleep), [[volver]] (return), [[encontrar]] (find), [[contar]] (tell/count), [[costar]] (cost), [[recordar]] (remember), [[morir]] (die). **jugar** is the only **u → ue**: [[juego]], [[juegas]].

**e → i** (only *-ir* verbs): [[pedir]] (ask for), [[repetir]] (repeat), [[servir]] (serve), [[seguir]] (follow — *sigo*), [[vestirse]] (get dressed).

- [[¿Puedes repetir, por favor?]] — Can you repeat, please?
- [[No entiendo.]] — I don't understand.
- [[¿Cuánto cuesta?]] — How much does it cost?
- [[Empiezo a trabajar a las nueve.]]
- [[Pienso que tienes razón.]]
- [[Pedimos dos cafés.]]

## Useful patterns

- **querer / poder / preferir + infinitive**: [[Quiero aprender español.]] [[¿Puedo pasar?]]
- **empezar a + infinitive**: [[Empieza a llover.]]
- **volver a + infinitive** = to do again: [[Vuelvo a llamar mañana.]]
- **pensar en** = to think about: [[Pienso en ti.]]

> The dictionary won't always warn you — learn these verbs with their *yo* form: *querer (quiero), poder (puedo), pedir (pido)*.

topics.title: Irregular yo forms; saber vs conocer
topics.md:
## Verbs irregular only in the yo form

Many common verbs are regular in the present **except for yo**:

| infinitive | yo | rest (regular) |
|---|---|---|
| [[hacer]] — to do, make | **hago** | haces, hace, hacemos… |
| [[poner]] — to put | **pongo** | pones, pone… |
| [[salir]] — to go out, leave | **salgo** | sales, sale… |
| [[traer]] — to bring | **traigo** | traes, trae… |
| [[caer]] — to fall | **caigo** | caes, cae… |
| [[saber]] — to know | **sé** | sabes, sabe… |
| [[ver]] — to see | **veo** | ves, ve… |
| [[dar]] — to give | **doy** | das, da, damos, dais, dan |
| [[conocer]] — to know (people/places) | **conozco** | conoces, conoce… |
| [[conducir]] — to drive | **conduzco** | conduces… |
| [[traducir]] — to translate | **traduzco** | traduces… |

Verbs in **-cer / -cir** after a vowel take **-zco**: *conozco, parezco, ofrezco, conduzco*.

## Irregular yo + stem change

| tener | venir | decir | oír |
|---|---|---|---|
| **tengo** | **vengo** | **digo** | **oigo** |
| tienes | vienes | dices | oyes |
| tiene | viene | dice | oye |
| tenemos | venimos | decimos | oímos |
| tenéis | venís | decís | oís |
| tienen | vienen | dicen | oyen |

## Saber vs conocer

Both mean *to know*, but:

| saber | conocer |
|---|---|
| facts, information: [[Sé su nombre.]] [[No sé dónde está.]] | people: [[Conozco a tu hermano.]] |
| how to do something (+ infinitive): [[Sé nadar.]] — I can swim. | places: [[¿Conoces Madrid?]] — Have you been to Madrid? |
| | be familiar with something: [[Conozco esta canción.]] |

> With people, **conocer a**: the "personal a" goes before a person who is a direct object: [[Conozco a María.]]

topics.title: Weather: hace, hay, está, llueve
topics.md:
## Talking about the weather

[[¿Qué tiempo hace?]] — What's the weather like? (*el tiempo* = both *time* and *weather*)

Spanish uses three verbs for weather:

**hacer** (+ noun) — for most general conditions:
| | |
|---|---|
| [[Hace calor.]] | It's hot. |
| [[Hace frío.]] | It's cold. |
| [[Hace sol.]] | It's sunny. |
| [[Hace viento.]] | It's windy. |
| [[Hace buen tiempo.]] / [[Hace mal tiempo.]] | The weather is good / bad. |
| [[Hace 30 grados.]] | It's 30 degrees. |

Because *calor, frío, sol* are nouns, "very" is **mucho**: [[Hace mucho calor.]] [[Hace mucho frío.]]

**estar** (+ adjective / gerund):
[[Está nublado.]] — It's cloudy. [[Está lloviendo.]] — It's raining (right now). [[Está despejado.]] — It's clear.

**hay** (+ noun): [[Hay niebla.]] (fog), [[Hay tormenta.]] (storm), [[Hay nubes.]]

**Weather verbs** used only in the 3rd person singular: [[llover]] → [[llueve]] (it rains), [[nevar]] → [[nieva]] (it snows).
[[En Londres llueve mucho.]] [[En invierno nieva en las montañas.]]

## Seasons

[[la primavera]] (spring) · [[el verano]] (summer) · [[el otoño]] (autumn) · [[el invierno]] (winter)
[[En verano hace mucho calor.]]

## People vs weather

| the weather | a person | a thing |
|---|---|---|
| [[Hace frío.]] | [[Tengo frío.]] — I'm cold. | [[El agua está fría.]] — The water is cold. |
| [[Hace calor.]] | [[Tengo calor.]] — I'm hot. | [[La sopa está caliente.]] — The soup is hot. |

drills.h: It rains a lot in London.

topics.title: Present progressive: estar + gerund
topics.md:
## Estar + gerund

To stress that something is happening **right now**, use **estar + gerund** (the *-ing* form):

| verb type | ending | example |
|---|---|---|
| -ar | **-ando** | hablar → [[hablando]] |
| -er / -ir | **-iendo** | comer → [[comiendo]], vivir → [[viviendo]] |

- [[Estoy hablando por teléfono.]] — I'm talking on the phone.
- [[¿Qué estás haciendo?]] — What are you doing?
- [[Están viendo una película.]]
- [[Está lloviendo.]] — It's raining.

## Irregular gerunds

| | |
|---|---|
| vowel + -er/-ir → **-yendo** | leer → [[leyendo]], oír → [[oyendo]], traer → [[trayendo]], ir → [[yendo]] |
| -ir stem change e → i | pedir → [[pidiendo]], decir → [[diciendo]], seguir → [[siguiendo]], vestir → [[vistiendo]] |
| -ir stem change o → u | dormir → [[durmiendo]], morir → [[muriendo]] |
| poder | [[pudiendo]] |

## Present vs present progressive

Spanish uses the progressive **less** than English. The simple present often covers "now":
[[¿Qué haces?]] = What are you doing? — perfectly natural.

Use *estar + gerund* to emphasize that the action is in progress or temporary:
[[Estoy trabajando en casa esta semana.]] — I'm working from home this week.

Never use it for the future (English *I'm leaving tomorrow* → [[Me voy mañana.]]) and avoid it with *ir, venir, tener, estar*.

## Pronouns

Object and reflexive pronouns go before *estar* or attach to the gerund (add an accent):
[[Me estoy duchando.]] = [[Estoy duchándome.]]

## Other gerund patterns

- **seguir + gerund** = to keep doing / still: [[Sigo estudiando español.]]
- **llevar + time + gerund** = to have been doing: [[Llevo dos años viviendo aquí.]] (more at B2)

topics.title: Comparisons: más/menos… que, tan… como
topics.md:
## More / less … than

| | |
|---|---|
| **más + adj. + que** | [[Madrid es más grande que Sevilla.]] — bigger than |
| **menos + adj. + que** | [[Este coche es menos caro que ese.]] — less expensive than |
| **tan + adj. + como** | [[Ana es tan alta como su madre.]] — as tall as |

The adjective still agrees with the noun: [[Mis hermanas son más altas que yo.]]

With **nouns**: **más / menos + noun + que**, and **tanto / tanta / tantos / tantas + noun + como**:
[[Tengo más libros que tú.]] [[No tengo tanto dinero como él.]] [[Hay tantas personas como ayer.]]

With **verbs**: **verb + más / menos que**, **verb + tanto como**:
[[Trabajo más que mi hermano.]] [[No como tanto como antes.]]

Before a number, "than" is **de**: [[Hay más de cien personas.]] — more than a hundred.

## Irregular comparatives

| | | |
|---|---|---|
| bueno / bien | **mejor** | better |
| malo / mal | **peor** | worse |
| grande (age) | **mayor** | older |
| pequeño (age) | **menor** | younger |

- [[Este restaurante es mejor que el otro.]]
- [[Hoy me siento peor.]]
- [[Mi hermano es mayor que yo.]] — My brother is older than me.
- [[Es dos años menor.]] — She's two years younger.

> For size, *más grande / más pequeño* are normal; *mayor / menor* are mostly for age (and for importance: *el problema mayor*).

Pronouns after *que / como* use subject forms: [[más alto que yo]], [[tan rápido como tú]].

## Clothes and shopping

[[¿Cuánto cuesta esta camisa?]] · [[¿Tiene una talla más grande?]] · [[Es demasiado cara.]] · [[Me la llevo.]] (I'll take it.) · [[¿Puedo probármelo?]] (Can I try it on?)

I don't have as much money as you.

drills.q: El hotel es ___ caro que la pensión.
El español es ___ difícil que el chino.
Tu idea es ___ que la mía.
Pedro es alto. Juan es bajo.
a: Pedro es más alto que Juan.

topics.title: Direct object pronouns (lo, la, los, las) and personal a
topics.md:
## Direct object pronouns

A direct object receives the action directly: *I see **the house*** → *I see **it***.

| | singular | plural |
|---|---|---|
| 1st | **me** — me | **nos** — us |
| 2nd | **te** — you | **os** — you all |
| 3rd masc. | **lo** — him, it, you (Ud.) | **los** — them, you (Uds.) |
| 3rd fem. | **la** — her, it, you (Ud.) | **las** — them, you (Uds.) |

The pronoun replaces the noun and agrees with it in **gender and number**:
- [[¿Tienes el libro? — Sí, lo tengo.]]
- [[¿Ves la casa? — Sí, la veo.]]
- [[¿Compras los zapatos? — No, no los compro.]]
- [[¿Conoces a mis hermanas? — Sí, las conozco.]]
- [[Te quiero.]] — I love you. [[¿Me ayudas?]] — Will you help me?

## Position

1. **Before a conjugated verb** (and before *no*): [[Lo veo.]] [[No lo veo.]]
2. **Attached to an infinitive or gerund**, or placed before the first verb — both are correct:
   [[Voy a comprarlo.]] = [[Lo voy a comprar.]]
   [[Estoy leyéndola.]] = [[La estoy leyendo.]] (add an accent to keep the stress)
3. **Attached to an affirmative command**: [[¡Cómelo!]] — Eat it! (but [[¡No lo comas!]])

## The personal a

When the direct object is a **specific person** (or a pet), put **a** in front of it:
[[Veo a María.]] [[Busco a mi hijo.]] [[Quiero a mi perro.]]
But not with things or unspecified people: [[Veo la casa.]] [[Busco un médico.]] And not after *tener*: [[Tengo dos hermanos.]]

## Lo as "it" for ideas

**lo** can stand for a whole idea: [[No lo sé.]] — I don't know (it). [[Lo siento.]] — I'm sorry. [[Ya lo veo.]] — I can see that.

> In parts of Spain you will hear *le* instead of *lo* for a male person (*le veo* = I see him). This is called *leísmo* and is accepted for people, but *lo* is always correct.

topics.title: Indirect object pronouns and se lo
topics.md:
## Indirect object pronouns

An indirect object is the person **to whom / for whom** something is done: *I give **him** the book*.

| | singular | plural |
|---|---|---|
| 1st | **me** — (to) me | **nos** — (to) us |
| 2nd | **te** — (to) you | **os** — (to) you all |
| 3rd | **le** — (to) him, her, you (Ud.) | **les** — (to) them, you (Uds.) |

Verbs of giving and communicating take indirect objects: *dar, regalar, mandar, enviar, prestar, decir, contar, explicar, enseñar, preguntar, escribir*.

- [[Le doy el libro.]] — I give him/her the book.
- [[¿Me prestas tu bolígrafo?]] — Can you lend me your pen?
- [[Les escribo una carta.]]
- [[Te explico la regla.]]

Spanish often keeps the pronoun **even when the person is named** — this is normal, not redundant:
[[Le doy el regalo a mi madre.]] [[Les digo la verdad a mis padres.]]

Position: the same as direct object pronouns (before the conjugated verb, attached to infinitive / gerund / affirmative command).

## Two pronouns together

When both appear, the **indirect comes first**: [[Me lo das.]] — You give it to me. [[Te la explico.]] — I'll explain it to you.

**le / les + lo / la / los / las → se lo / se la / se los / se las**
(*le lo* doesn't exist in Spanish.)

| | |
|---|---|
| [[Le doy el libro.]] | → [[Se lo doy.]] — I give it to him. |
| [[Les mando las fotos.]] | → [[Se las mando.]] — I send them to them. |
| [[Voy a dárselo.]] | I'm going to give it to him/her. (note the accent) |

Because *se* can mean him, her, them or you, add *a + person* if needed: [[Se lo doy a ella.]]

We send them (las fotos) to you (tú).
He explains it (la regla) to us.
I'm going to give it to her.

drills.q: Mando las cartas a mis padres.
¿Le diste el dinero a Juan? — Sí, ___ di.

topics.title: Preterite: regular verbs
topics.md:
## The preterite (pretérito indefinido)

The preterite describes **completed actions in the past** — things that happened at a specific moment or within a closed period: *yesterday, last year, in 2010, three times*.

| | -ar: hablar | -er: comer | -ir: vivir |
|---|---|---|---|
| yo | habl**é** | com**í** | viv**í** |
| tú | habl**aste** | com**iste** | viv**iste** |
| él/ella/Ud. | habl**ó** | com**ió** | viv**ió** |
| nosotros | habl**amos** | com**imos** | viv**imos** |
| vosotros | habl**asteis** | com**isteis** | viv**isteis** |
| ellos/Uds. | habl**aron** | com**ieron** | viv**ieron** |

- **-er and -ir** share the same endings.
- The accents on **-é, -ó, -í, -ió** matter: [[hablo]] (I speak) vs [[habló]] (he spoke).
- *nosotros* of -ar and -ir verbs is the same as the present (*hablamos, vivimos*) — context tells you which.

Examples:
- [[Ayer trabajé diez horas.]]
- [[¿Comiste en casa?]]
- [[Vivimos en París dos años.]]
- [[El año pasado visitaron México.]]
- [[Nací en 1990.]]

## Spelling changes in the yo form

To keep the sound of the consonant:
| | | |
|---|---|---|
| -car → **-qué** | buscar | [[busqué]] |
| -gar → **-gué** | llegar, pagar | [[llegué]], [[pagué]] |
| -zar → **-cé** | empezar | [[empecé]] |

Vowel + -er/-ir → **-yó, -yeron**: leer → [[leyó]], [[leyeron]]; oír → [[oyó]]; caer → [[cayó]].

## Time expressions with the preterite

[[ayer]] · [[anoche]] (last night) · [[anteayer]] · [[el lunes pasado]] · [[la semana pasada]] · [[el año pasado]] · [[hace dos días]] (two days ago) · [[en 2015]] · [[de repente]] (suddenly)

topics.title: Preterite: irregular verbs
topics.md:
## Irregular preterites

The most common verbs are irregular in the preterite. Good news: most of them share **one set of endings** (with no accents!) on an irregular stem.

**Endings:** -e, -iste, -o, -imos, -isteis, -ieron

| infinitive | stem | yo | él/ella | ellos |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| tener | **tuv-** | [[tuve]] | [[tuvo]] | tuvieron |
| estar | **estuv-** | [[estuve]] | [[estuvo]] | estuvieron |
| andar | **anduv-** | anduve | anduvo | anduvieron |
| poder | **pud-** | [[pude]] | [[pudo]] | pudieron |
| poner | **pus-** | [[puse]] | [[puso]] | pusieron |
| saber | **sup-** | [[supe]] | [[supo]] | supieron |
| hacer | **hic-** | [[hice]] | [[hizo]] (c→z) | hicieron |
| querer | **quis-** | [[quise]] | [[quiso]] | quisieron |
| venir | **vin-** | [[vine]] | [[vino]] | vinieron |
| decir | **dij-** | [[dije]] | [[dijo]] | **dijeron** |
| traer | **traj-** | [[traje]] | [[trajo]] | **trajeron** |
| conducir | **conduj-** | conduje | condujo | **condujeron** |

Stems ending in **-j** drop the *i*: *dijeron, trajeron* (not *dijieron*).

## Ser and ir — identical!

| | ser / ir |
|---|---|
| yo | [[fui]] |
| tú | [[fuiste]] |
| él/ella/Ud. | [[fue]] |
| nosotros | [[fuimos]] |
| vosotros | [[fuisteis]] |
| ellos/Uds. | [[fueron]] |

Context makes it clear: [[Fui al cine.]] (I went) vs [[Fue un día increíble.]] (It was).

## Dar and ver

[[di]], diste, [[dio]], dimos, disteis, dieron · [[vi]], viste, [[vio]], vimos, visteis, vieron — no accents.

## -ir stem-changers (3rd person only)

-ir verbs with a present stem change also change in **él/ella and ellos**: **e → i**, **o → u**.
pedir → [[pidió]], [[pidieron]]; sentir → [[sintió]]; dormir → [[durmió]], [[durmieron]]; morir → [[murió]].

## Meaning changes

Some verbs shift meaning in the preterite: [[supe]] = I found out; [[conocí]] = I met (for the first time); [[no quise]] = I refused; [[pude]] = I managed to.

drills.q: Nosotros ___ (estar) en casa todo el día.

topics.title: The imperfect
topics.md:
## The imperfect (pretérito imperfecto)

The imperfect describes the past as **ongoing, habitual or background**: what things *were like*, what people *used to do*, what *was happening*.

| | -ar: hablar | -er: comer | -ir: vivir |
|---|---|---|---|
| yo | habl**aba** | com**ía** | viv**ía** |
| tú | habl**abas** | com**ías** | viv**ías** |
| él/ella/Ud. | habl**aba** | com**ía** | viv**ía** |
| nosotros | habl**ábamos** | com**íamos** | viv**íamos** |
| vosotros | habl**abais** | com**íais** | viv**íais** |
| ellos/Uds. | habl**aban** | com**ían** | viv**ían** |

*yo* and *él/ella* are identical — add the pronoun if needed.

## Only three irregular verbs

| ser | ir | ver |
|---|---|---|
| [[era]] | [[iba]] | [[veía]] |
| eras | ibas | veías |
| era | iba | veía |
| éramos | íbamos | veíamos |
| erais | ibais | veíais |
| eran | iban | veían |

**hay → había** (there was / there were): [[Había mucha gente.]]

## Uses

1. **Habits in the past** — *used to / would*: [[Cuando era niño, jugaba al fútbol todos los días.]]
2. **Descriptions** of people, places, weather, time and age: [[La casa era grande y tenía un jardín.]] [[Hacía frío.]] [[Eran las diez.]] [[Tenía veinte años.]]
3. **Actions in progress** (*was doing*): [[Mientras yo cocinaba, ella leía.]]
4. **Feelings and states**: [[Estaba cansado.]] [[Quería ir, pero no podía.]]
5. **Polite requests**: [[Quería un café, por favor.]] — I'd like a coffee.

## Signal words

[[siempre]] · [[a menudo]] · [[a veces]] · [[todos los días]] · [[cada verano]] · [[normalmente]] · [[antes]] (before, in the past) · [[de niño]] / [[cuando era pequeño]] (as a child) · [[mientras]] (while)

**soler** in the imperfect = *used to*: [[Solía levantarme temprano.]]

drills.q: Nosotros ___ (ir) a la playa cada verano.
Yo ___ (ver) la tele todas las noches.

topics.title: Preterite or imperfect?
topics.md:
## Two past tenses, two perspectives

Choosing between the preterite and the imperfect is about **how you look at the past action**, not about how long it lasted.

| preterite | imperfect |
|---|---|
| completed event, with a beginning or end | ongoing, unfinished, background |
| *what happened* | *what was going on / what it was like* |
| [[Ayer llovió.]] — It rained yesterday (a complete event). | [[Llovía.]] — It was raining (scene-setting). |
| [[Trabajé allí cinco años.]] — closed period | [[Trabajaba allí.]] — I used to work / was working there |
| [[Fui a Roma en 2019.]] | [[Iba a Roma cada verano.]] |

## Stories: background + events

In a story, the **imperfect paints the scene**, the **preterite moves the plot forward**:

[[Era un sábado por la noche. Hacía frío y yo estaba en casa. De repente, sonó el teléfono. Era mi hermano.]]

The classic combination — an action in progress **interrupted** by another:
- [[Estaba en la ducha cuando llegó el correo.]]
- [[Mientras dormíamos, entró un ladrón.]]
- [[Cuando salí, llovía.]] (it was raining when I left)

## Signal words (tendencies, not rules)

| usually preterite | usually imperfect |
|---|---|
| ayer, anoche, el año pasado | siempre, a menudo, a veces |
| una vez, dos veces | todos los días, cada semana |
| de repente, en ese momento | mientras, normalmente |
| en 2010, durante tres horas | de niño, antes |

## Verbs that change meaning

| | preterite | imperfect |
|---|---|---|
| conocer | [[Conocí a Ana en 2015.]] — I **met** | [[Conocía a Ana.]] — I **knew** |
| saber | [[Supe la verdad.]] — I **found out** | [[Sabía la verdad.]] — I **knew** |
| querer | [[No quise ir.]] — I **refused** | [[No quería ir.]] — I **didn't want** |
| poder | [[Pude terminar.]] — I **managed** | [[Podía terminar.]] — I **was able** |
| tener | [[Tuve una idea.]] — I **got** an idea | [[Tenía una idea.]] — I **had** |

drills.q: Cuando era niño, ___ al parque todos los días.
Ayer ___ al parque con mi hermano.
___ las nueve cuando empezó la película.
Antes ___ en Londres, ahora vivo en Madrid.
___ a mi novia en una fiesta en 2018.
La casa ___ grande y tenía un jardín.
Estaba en la ducha cuando ___ mi madre.
Normalmente ___ el autobús, pero ese día tomé un taxi.
Ella ___ la verdad ayer por la noche.

topics.title: Por and para
topics.md:
Both often translate as *for*, but they look in different directions: **para** points **forward** to a goal or destination; **por** looks **back** at a cause, or describes the route / means / exchange.

## Para

| use | example |
|---|---|
| purpose (*in order to*) + infinitive | [[Estudio para aprender.]] |
| recipient | [[Este regalo es para ti.]] |
| destination | [[Salgo para Madrid.]] — I'm leaving for Madrid. |
| deadline | [[Lo necesito para el lunes.]] — by Monday |
| opinion | [[Para mí, es fácil.]] — In my opinion… |
| comparison with expectation | [[Para ser niño, habla muy bien.]] — for a child… |
| employer | [[Trabajo para una empresa alemana.]] |
| use of an object | [[una taza para café]] |

## Por

| use | example |
|---|---|
| cause, reason (*because of*) | [[Lo hago por ti.]] — I do it because of / for your sake. |
| through, along, around (movement) | [[Paseamos por el parque.]] [[Entró por la ventana.]] |
| approximate time / part of day | [[por la mañana]], [[por la noche]] |
| duration | [[Estudié por dos horas.]] (often just *dos horas*) |
| exchange, price | [[Lo compré por diez euros.]] [[Gracias por todo.]] |
| means of communication / transport | [[por teléfono]], [[por correo]], [[por avión]] |
| agent in the passive | [[escrito por Cervantes]] |
| per | [[cien kilómetros por hora]], [[dos veces por semana]] |
| on behalf of / in place of | [[¿Puedes trabajar por mí mañana?]] |

## Fixed expressions with por

[[por favor]] · [[por eso]] (that's why) · [[por fin]] (finally) · [[por ejemplo]] · [[por supuesto]] (of course) · [[por lo menos]] (at least) · [[por cierto]] (by the way) · [[por si acaso]] (just in case) · [[por qué]] (why) / **para qué** (what for)

> Quick test: if you can say *in order to* or *destined for*, use **para**. If you can say *because of, through, in exchange for, by*, use **por**.

drills.q: El tren sale ___ Sevilla a las diez.
Voy a la farmacia ___ comprar aspirinas.
No fui a clase ___ la lluvia.
El libro fue escrito ___ García Márquez.
Voy al gimnasio tres veces ___ semana.

topics.title: Present perfect (he hablado)
topics.md:
## Present perfect: he hablado

**haber** (present) + **past participle**:

| haber | + participle |
|---|---|
| yo **he** | hablado |
| tú **has** | comido |
| él/ella/Ud. **ha** | vivido |
| nosotros **hemos** | |
| vosotros **habéis** | |
| ellos/Uds. **han** | |

**Participles:** -ar → **-ado** ([[hablado]]), -er / -ir → **-ido** ([[comido]], [[vivido]]). The participle never changes after *haber*, and nothing goes between *haber* and the participle: [[No lo he visto.]]

## Irregular participles (learn these!)

| | | | |
|---|---|---|---|
| hacer → [[hecho]] | decir → [[dicho]] | ver → [[visto]] | escribir → [[escrito]] |
| poner → [[puesto]] | volver → [[vuelto]] | abrir → [[abierto]] | romper → [[roto]] |
| morir → [[muerto]] | descubrir → [[descubierto]] | resolver → [[resuelto]] | ir → [[ido]] |

Vowel + -ído: leer → [[leído]], oír → [[oído]], traer → [[traído]].

## When to use it

1. **Experiences** (ever / never): [[¿Has estado en México? — No, nunca he estado allí.]]
2. Actions in a **time period that is still open**: [[Hoy he trabajado mucho.]] [[Esta semana hemos ido al cine dos veces.]] [[Este año he viajado poco.]]
3. **Recent past** with present relevance (especially in Spain): [[¿Qué ha pasado?]] [[He perdido las llaves.]]
4. With **ya** (already), **todavía no / aún no** (not yet), **nunca**, **alguna vez** (ever): [[Ya he comido.]] [[Todavía no he terminado.]]

## Present perfect vs preterite

| present perfect (period not over) | preterite (period over) |
|---|---|
| [[Hoy he visto a Juan.]] | [[Ayer vi a Juan.]] |
| [[Este mes he leído tres libros.]] | [[El mes pasado leí tres libros.]] |

> In most of **Latin America** the preterite is used even for "today" and recent events: *¿Qué pasó?* instead of *¿Qué ha pasado?* Both are correct; Spain prefers the perfect for today.

drills.h: Have you ever been to Peru?
Put it in the present perfect

topics.title: The future tense
topics.md:
## The simple future

Take the **whole infinitive** and add the endings — the same for -ar, -er and -ir:

| | hablar |
|---|---|
| yo | hablar**é** |
| tú | hablar**ás** |
| él/ella/Ud. | hablar**á** |
| nosotros | hablar**emos** |
| vosotros | hablar**éis** |
| ellos/Uds. | hablar**án** |

[[Mañana lloverá.]] [[¿Vendrás a la fiesta?]] [[Algún día viviremos en la playa.]]

## Irregular stems (same endings)

| | stem | yo |
|---|---|---|
| tener | **tendr-** | [[tendré]] |
| poner | **pondr-** | [[pondré]] |
| salir | **saldr-** | [[saldré]] |
| venir | **vendr-** | [[vendré]] |
| poder | **podr-** | [[podré]] |
| saber | **sabr-** | [[sabré]] |
| haber | **habr-** | [[habrá]] (there will be) |
| querer | **querr-** | [[querré]] |
| hacer | **har-** | [[haré]] |
| decir | **dir-** | [[diré]] |

## Future vs ir a + infinitive

| ir a + infinitive | simple future |
|---|---|
| plans and intentions, everyday speech | predictions, promises, formal or distant future |
| [[Voy a cenar con Ana esta noche.]] | [[Te llamaré mañana, te lo prometo.]] |
| [[Va a llover.]] (I can see the clouds) | [[En el futuro, los coches serán eléctricos.]] |

The **present tense** is also used for scheduled events: [[El tren sale a las ocho.]]

## Future of probability

The future also expresses a **guess about the present**: [[¿Qué hora será? — Serán las tres.]] (I wonder what time it is. — It must be about three.) [[Estará en casa.]] — He's probably at home. (More at B1.)

## Time expressions

[[mañana]] · [[pasado mañana]] · [[la semana que viene]] / [[la próxima semana]] · [[el año que viene]] · [[dentro de dos días]] (in two days) · [[pronto]] · [[algún día]]

drills.q: El año que viene nosotros ___ (vivir) en Chile.

topics.title: The conditional
topics.md:
## The conditional — would

Like the future: **infinitive + endings**. The endings are the same as the imperfect of -er/-ir verbs.

| | hablar |
|---|---|
| yo | hablar**ía** |
| tú | hablar**ías** |
| él/ella/Ud. | hablar**ía** |
| nosotros | hablar**íamos** |
| vosotros | hablar**íais** |
| ellos/Uds. | hablar**ían** |

**Irregular stems** are exactly the same as in the future: *tendría, pondría, saldría, vendría, podría, sabría, habría, querría, haría, diría*.

## Uses

1. **Polite requests**: [[¿Podría ayudarme?]] — Could you help me? [[Me gustaría un café.]] — I'd like a coffee. [[¿Te importaría cerrar la ventana?]]
2. **Advice** (*should*): [[Deberías descansar.]] [[Yo que tú, no lo haría.]] — If I were you, I wouldn't do it. [[En tu lugar, hablaría con él.]]
3. **Wishes and hypotheses**: [[Me encantaría vivir en Barcelona.]] [[Con más dinero, viajaría por todo el mundo.]]
4. **Future in the past** (reported speech): [[Dijo que vendría.]] — He said he would come.
5. **Guess about the past**: [[Serían las diez cuando llegó.]] — It was probably around ten. (More at B1.)

> **would** meaning *used to* is the **imperfect**, not the conditional: *When I was a child I would play outside* → [[De niño jugaba fuera.]]

Full *if*-sentences (*If I had money, I would…*) need the imperfect subjunctive — you'll learn them at B1: [[Si tuviera dinero, viajaría.]]

drills.h: When I was a child I would play outside.

topics.title: Commands: tú and usted (affirmative)
topics.md:
## Affirmative commands

**tú** (informal): the same as the *él/ella* form of the present:
hablar → [[¡Habla!]], comer → [[¡Come!]], escribir → [[¡Escribe!]]

**usted / ustedes** (formal): swap the vowel — -ar verbs take **-e / -en**, -er/-ir verbs take **-a / -an** (these are present subjunctive forms):

| | tú | usted | ustedes |
|---|---|---|---|
| hablar | habla | **hable** | **hablen** |
| comer | come | **coma** | **coman** |
| escribir | escribe | **escriba** | **escriban** |
| tener | **ten** | **tenga** | **tengan** |
| hacer | **haz** | **haga** | **hagan** |

The *usted* form is built from the **yo** form: *tengo → tenga, hago → haga, pido → pida, digo → diga, conozco → conozca*.

## Irregular tú commands

| | | | |
|---|---|---|---|
| decir → [[di]] | hacer → [[haz]] | ir → [[ve]] | poner → [[pon]] |
| salir → [[sal]] | ser → [[sé]] | tener → [[ten]] | venir → [[ven]] |

**vosotros** (Spain): replace -r of the infinitive with **-d**: [[hablad]], [[comed]], [[venid]].

## Pronouns attach to affirmative commands

[[¡Dímelo!]] (Tell me it!) [[Siéntese, por favor.]] [[Cómelo.]] [[Levántate.]] — add an accent to keep the original stress.
Reflexive *vosotros* drops the -d: *sentad + os → sentaos*.

## Recipes and directions

| | |
|---|---|
| [[Siga recto.]] | Go straight on. |
| [[Gire a la derecha / a la izquierda.]] | Turn right / left. |
| [[Tome la segunda calle.]] | Take the second street. |
| [[Cruce la plaza.]] | Cross the square. |
| [[Corte las cebollas.]] | Chop the onions. |
| [[Añada sal.]] | Add salt. |
| [[Mezcle bien.]] | Mix well. |

> **Negative commands** (*don't…*) use a different form for *tú* (*¡No hables!*). They come at B1 with the subjunctive. Softer alternatives: [[¿Puedes cerrar la puerta?]] / [[¿Me pasas la sal?]]

topics.title: Doler, parecer, interesar: more verbs like gustar
topics.md:
## Verbs like gustar

Several common verbs work like *gustar*: the person is an indirect object (*me, te, le…*) and the verb agrees with the **thing**.

| verb | meaning | example |
|---|---|---|
| [[doler]] (o→ue) | to hurt | [[Me duele la cabeza.]] — I have a headache. |
| [[encantar]] | to love (things) | [[Me encantan los museos.]] |
| [[interesar]] | to interest | [[¿Te interesa la política?]] |
| [[importar]] | to matter, to mind | [[No me importa.]] — I don't mind. |
| [[molestar]] | to bother | [[Me molesta el ruido.]] |
| [[parecer]] | to seem | [[¿Qué te parece?]] — What do you think? |
| [[faltar]] | to be missing, lack | [[Me falta tiempo.]] |
| [[quedar]] | to have left; to suit | [[Nos quedan dos días.]] [[Te queda bien.]] |
| [[apetecer]] (Spain) | to feel like | [[¿Te apetece un café?]] |

- [[Me duelen los pies.]] — My feet hurt. (plural → *duelen*)
- [[A mi madre le duele la espalda.]]
- [[Me parece una buena idea.]] — I think it's a good idea.

## Health

[[¿Qué te pasa?]] — What's wrong? [[¿Cómo te encuentras?]] — How are you feeling?

| | |
|---|---|
| [[Tengo fiebre.]] | I have a fever. |
| [[Tengo dolor de cabeza / estómago / garganta.]] | I have a headache / stomachache / sore throat. |
| [[Estoy resfriado.]] | I have a cold. |
| [[Tengo gripe.]] | I have the flu. |
| [[Me siento mal.]] | I feel ill. |
| [[Tengo tos.]] | I have a cough. |

## The body

[[la cabeza]] · [[el ojo]] · [[la oreja]] / [[el oído]] (outer / inner ear) · [[la nariz]] · [[la boca]] · [[el diente]] · [[la garganta]] · [[el cuello]] · [[la espalda]] · [[el pecho]] · [[el estómago]] · [[el brazo]] · [[la mano]] · [[el dedo]] · [[la pierna]] · [[la rodilla]] · [[el pie]]

> Spanish uses **the**, not *my*, with body parts when the owner is clear: [[Me duele la mano.]] — My hand hurts.

topics.title: Algo, nada, alguien, nadie, alguno, ninguno
topics.md:
## Positive and negative words

| positive | negative |
|---|---|
| [[algo]] — something, anything | [[nada]] — nothing |
| [[alguien]] — someone, anyone | [[nadie]] — nobody |
| [[alguno]] / alguna / algunos / algunas — some, any | [[ninguno]] / ninguna — no, none |
| [[siempre]] — always | [[nunca]] / [[jamás]] — never |
| [[también]] — also | [[tampoco]] — neither |
| [[o… o]] — either… or | [[ni… ni]] — neither… nor |

- [[¿Quieres algo? — No, no quiero nada.]]
- [[¿Hay alguien en casa? — No, no hay nadie.]]
- [[¿Tienes algún libro en español? — No, no tengo ninguno.]]

## Double negation is correct

If the negative word comes **after** the verb, put **no** before the verb. If it comes **before**, don't use *no*:
[[No viene nadie.]] = [[Nadie viene.]] · [[No como nunca carne.]] = [[Nunca como carne.]]
You can even stack them: [[No digo nunca nada a nadie.]] — I never say anything to anyone.

## Alguno / ninguno

They agree with the noun and shorten before a masculine singular noun: **algún**, **ningún**:
[[algún día]] (some day), [[alguna vez]] (ever, once), [[algunos amigos]], [[ningún problema]], [[ninguna idea]].
*Ninguno* is almost always singular: [[No tengo ningún amigo aquí.]]

## Todo, cada, cualquier

- **todo / toda / todos / todas** + article: [[todo el día]] (all day), [[todos los días]] (every day), [[toda la gente]].
- **todo** alone = everything: [[Lo sé todo.]]
- **cada** (each, every — never changes): [[cada semana]], [[cada uno]].
- **cualquier** + noun = any (whatever): [[Llámame a cualquier hora.]]; alone: **cualquiera** = anyone, any one.

## Otro

[[otro libro]] (another book — never *un otro*), [[otra vez]] (again), [[los otros]] (the others).

a: No hay nadie en la puerta.

topics.title: Possessive pronouns (mío, tuyo, suyo…)
topics.md:
## Mine, yours, his…

Long (stressed) possessives agree with the **thing owned**:

| owner | masc. sing. | fem. sing. | masc. pl. | fem. pl. |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| yo | **mío** | **mía** | **míos** | **mías** |
| tú | **tuyo** | **tuya** | **tuyos** | **tuyas** |
| él / ella / Ud. | **suyo** | **suya** | **suyos** | **suyas** |
| nosotros | **nuestro** | **nuestra** | **nuestros** | **nuestras** |
| vosotros | **vuestro** | **vuestra** | **vuestros** | **vuestras** |
| ellos / Uds. | **suyo** | **suya** | **suyos** | **suyas** |

## Three ways to use them

1. **After ser** (no article): [[Este libro es mío.]] — This book is mine. [[¿Es tuya esta maleta?]]
2. **As pronouns with an article** (to replace a noun): [[Tu coche es rojo; el mío es azul.]] — Your car is red; mine is blue. [[Mis padres viven en Madrid. ¿Y los tuyos?]]
3. **After a noun** (*of mine*): [[un amigo mío]] — a friend of mine. [[¡Dios mío!]] — My God!

**suyo** is ambiguous (his, hers, theirs, yours) — clarify with *de*: [[el de ella]], [[el de ustedes]].

## Lo mío / lo tuyo

The neuter **lo** + possessive = *my thing / what's mine*: [[Lo mío es la música.]] — Music is my thing.

## Everyday objects

[[la maleta]] (suitcase) · [[el bolso]] (handbag) · [[la cartera]] (wallet) · [[las llaves]] · [[el móvil]] / [[el celular]] (mobile phone) · [[las gafas]] (glasses) · [[el paraguas]] (umbrella)

drills.q: Tu coche es rojo; el ___ es azul.
drills.h: Your car is red; mine is blue.
My parents live here. And yours? (tú)

drills.q: Mi casa es grande, pero la ___ es más grande.

topics.title: Superlatives and -ísimo
topics.md:
## The most / the least

**el / la / los / las (+ noun) + más / menos + adjective (+ de)**

- [[Es el chico más alto de la clase.]] — He's the tallest boy in the class.
- [[Es la ciudad más bonita del mundo.]]
- [[Este es el libro menos interesante.]]
- [[Son los mejores amigos del mundo.]]

Notice: *in / of the* after a superlative is **de**, not *en*.

## Irregular superlatives

[[el mejor]] (the best) · [[el peor]] (the worst) · [[el mayor]] (the oldest / biggest) · [[el menor]] (the youngest) — they go **before** the noun:
[[Es la mejor película del año.]] [[Mi hermano mayor]] — my older brother. [[el peor día de mi vida]]

## Absolute superlative: -ísimo

To say *very, extremely*, add **-ísimo / -ísima / -ísimos / -ísimas** (drop the final vowel):

| | |
|---|---|
| grande → [[grandísimo]] | caro → [[carísimo]] |
| bueno → [[buenísimo]] | fácil → [[facilísimo]] |
| guapo → [[guapísima]] | mucho → [[muchísimo]] |

Spelling: *rico → riquísimo, largo → larguísimo, feliz → felicísimo*.

[[La comida está buenísima.]] — The food is really good. [[Muchísimas gracias.]] — Thank you so much.

## Describing places and things

[[famoso]] · [[importante]] · [[interesante]] · [[aburrido]] · [[divertido]] · [[peligroso]] · [[tranquilo]] · [[ruidoso]] · [[rico]] / [[pobre]]

drills.q: Es el chico más alto ___ la clase.
Es la ciudad ___ bonita del país.
Fue el ___ día de mi vida.
Es el restaurante ___ caro de la ciudad.

topics.title: Adverbs: -mente, muy, mucho, bastante, demasiado
topics.md:
## Adverbs in -mente

Take the **feminine** form of the adjective and add **-mente** (= English *-ly*):

| adjective | adverb |
|---|---|
| rápido → rápida | [[rápidamente]] |
| lento → lenta | [[lentamente]] |
| fácil | [[fácilmente]] |
| tranquilo → tranquila | [[tranquilamente]] |
| real | [[realmente]] |
| claro → clara | [[claramente]] |

The adjective keeps its written accent: *rápidamente, fácilmente*.
With two adverbs in a row, only the last takes *-mente*: [[Habla clara y lentamente.]]

Many everyday adverbs don't end in *-mente*: [[bien]], [[mal]], [[despacio]] (slowly), [[deprisa]] (quickly), [[rápido]] (also used as an adverb: *¡Ven rápido!*), [[pronto]] (soon), [[tarde]], [[temprano]], [[casi]] (almost), [[solo]] (only), [[ya]], [[todavía]].

## Muy or mucho?

| **muy** + adjective / adverb | **mucho** + noun / after a verb |
|---|---|
| [[muy bonito]], [[muy bien]], [[muy tarde]] | [[mucho dinero]], [[muchas personas]] |
| | [[Trabajo mucho.]] — I work a lot. |

*mucho* before a noun agrees (*mucha agua, muchos libros*); after a verb it never changes.
Exceptions: **mejor, peor, mayor, menor, más, menos** take *mucho*: [[mucho mejor]], [[mucho más caro]].

## Degree

[[demasiado]] (too, too much): [[Es demasiado caro.]] [[Comes demasiado.]] · [[bastante]] (quite, enough): [[Es bastante difícil.]] · [[un poco]] (a bit): [[Estoy un poco cansado.]] · [[nada]] (not at all): [[No es nada fácil.]]

## Frequency

[[siempre]] · [[casi siempre]] · [[normalmente]] / [[generalmente]] · [[a menudo]] (often) · [[a veces]] (sometimes) · [[de vez en cuando]] (from time to time) · [[casi nunca]] · [[nunca]]

Position: frequency adverbs usually go before the verb or at the end: [[A veces voy al cine.]] [[Voy al cine a veces.]]

topics.title: Relative pronouns: que, quien, donde, lo que
topics.md:
## Que — the all-purpose relative

**que** (no accent) means *who, which, that* and works for people and things. Unlike English, it can **never be left out**.

- [[El libro que leo es interesante.]] — The book (that) I'm reading is interesting.
- [[La chica que vive aquí es mi prima.]] — The girl who lives here…
- [[Las fotos que me enviaste son preciosas.]]

## Quien / quienes — for people

Used for people **after a preposition** (*with whom, to whom…*) or in non-essential clauses between commas:
- [[La persona con quien hablé era muy amable.]] — The person I talked to…
- [[Mi hermano, quien vive en Lima, viene mañana.]]
- At the start of a sentence = *whoever*: [[Quien busca, encuentra.]]

## Donde — where

[[La ciudad donde nací es pequeña.]] — The city where I was born… [[el restaurante donde comimos]]

## Lo que — what (the thing that)

[[Lo que necesito es dormir.]] — What I need is to sleep. [[No entiendo lo que dices.]] — I don't understand what you're saying. [[Haz lo que quieras.]] — Do what you want.

Compare with the question word **qué**: [[¿Qué dices?]] (What are you saying?) vs [[No sé qué dices.]] (indirect question: accent!) — but *lo que* has no accent.

## Prepositions come first

English can leave a preposition at the end (*the man I spoke **to***), Spanish cannot:
[[el hombre con quien hablé]], [[la casa en la que vivo]], [[el amigo de quien te hablé]].

After a preposition, *que* usually needs an article: **el que, la que, los que, las que** (you'll study these more at B1).

## Useful nouns

[[la persona]] · [[el sitio]] / [[el lugar]] (place) · [[la cosa]] · [[la manera]] / [[la forma]] (way) · [[la razón]] (reason)

La persona con ___ hablé es mi jefa.
La chica ___ vive aquí es mi prima.

the friends with whom I travel
